articles.title: Ice Frost Feather
articles.summary: Frost fern crystals with sharp clearcoat feather branches, icy sparkle on a smooth base. Reads as a clean smooth sheen with only a hint of fine glints; no frost fern shows.
articles.what: Frost fern crystals with sharp clearcoat feather branches. Up close: Very faint: a sparse scatter of tiny bright dashes and dots, mostly in short horizontal streaks, on an otherwise smooth surface. The fern or feather branches of the description are not visible at 1:1. From a distance: Reads as a clean smooth sheen with only a hint of fine glints; no frost fern shows. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Definitive Spec Replacements (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
when: Best on: body, roof, hero panel.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Definitive Spec Replacements", or search for "Ice Frost Feather".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood and roof: where frost would naturally form
Broad panels; too faint to matter on trim
Numbers keep their colour; effect is too faint to affect legibility.
Almost nothing: a few glints in the highlight
Pairs well with: gloss, matte, metallic.
pitfalls: Not a white frost coating: it adds no colour, only micro shine specks
Not visible fern crystals: branches do not show at this scale
Avoid: subtle on light bases, reads as smudge at distance.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.

examples.title: Add it as an overlay
examples.goal: Layer Ice Frost Feather over a base finish.
examples.result: The shine of the zone gets this texture while the colours stay put.

articles.title: Sandblasted Mask Edge
articles.summary: Tight satin grain with a hard tape edge; subtle matte-to-gloss transition, near-invisible at range. Reads as plain finish, perhaps a touch of satin frost.
articles.what: Masked blast transitions, satin eroded grain, and sharp tape borders. Up close: A very fine, soft, even micro-grain, finer and gentler than coarse sandblast, hard to see on satin and visible as a light frosted sheen on metal in the highlight. No tape edge, border or transition is visible in this crop. From a distance: Reads as plain finish, perhaps a touch of satin frost. No colour change. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Definitive Spec Replacements (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
